signals.title: The decision-model land rush: Cloudflare, Amazon, OpenAI, and Perplexity all ship cheap agent-verifier models in one week
signals.summary: A week after last week's CLM-8B spark, the category exploded: Cloudflare released Clef (27B/9B, Apache 2.0, beats rival Jev on 3 of 4 workflow evals, 39ms latency), Amazon shipped Strands Decider (2B params, full weights/data/training scripts, 153ms on an M3 MacBook CPU), OpenAI launched a Decisions API, Perplexity released pplx-decider-v1-27b, and Jared Palmer's open Kev family (0.8B-27B) rounded it out. These models don't generate text at all, they read state plus a schema of options and return probabilities, so agent routing/validation now costs near-zero and runs near-instant. An HN pushback post (98 pts) arguing decision models don't beat LLM-as-judge is itself corroboration of how fast this became a real debate.
signals.run_with_it_note: Every multi-step skill David runs (radar, morning-brief, kid-coach, content-gate) currently burns a full LLM call for small yes/no or classify decisions inside the pipeline. Pull Cloudflare's Clef-flash (open weights, Apache 2.0) and swap it in for one such checkpoint, e.g. the content-gate pass/fail band or a kid-coach approval-intent classifier, and clock the latency/cost difference against the current LLM-as-judge call.

signals.title: Strata: a 125B-parameter model running usable-speed, fully local, on a single gaming GPU
signals.summary: An MIT-licensed inference engine (built on llama.cpp/ggml plus ISTA-DASLab/Unsloth compression) runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125-billion-parameter model, on a single RTX 20-50 series or Radeon RX 7800/7900+ card with just 12GB VRAM, hitting 94 tok/s generation and 2,650 tok/s prompt processing on an RTX 5070. Install is a double-click .bat/.sh, no cloud account, no API key. 844 points on HN's front page.
signals.run_with_it_note: A frontier-class 125B model on a $500 consumer GPU with zero per-token cost changes the math on any task David currently pays a metered API for. Cheap first test: grab one spare gaming PC (or rent a single RTX 4090 hour on Vast.ai/RunPod), run Strata's installer, and point it at one real recurring job, like drafting the first pass of a review reply or a morning-brief summarization step, then compare output quality and cost against the current API call.

signals.title: Starlink opens a host program: get paid to sell hourly/daily/weekly internet passes at your site
signals.summary: SpaceX is recruiting beta hosts for 'Starlink for Communities': install one Starlink kit at a site, Starlink handles payment and access, and nearby people buy an Hour/Day/Week pass (one device) or a Month pass (up to 4 devices) instead of running their own subscription. Target hosts named explicitly: apartment complexes, campgrounds, rural areas, and local entrepreneurs/property owners. No US pricing or GA date yet, but the host-interest beta is open now. Corroborated across PCMag, Yahoo Finance, Telecompetitor, RVTravel, and TeslaNorth.
signals.run_with_it_note: David already owns the exact asset class this targets: marina docks, put-in spots, and campground-adjacent tour sites, several in rural/weak-signal water areas where a single Starlink kit would be a real customer amenity, not a novelty. First move costs nothing but a form: apply as a beta host for one site (a Door County or Buffalo Bayou dock is the obvious test) and see what Starlink actually pays per pass before committing hardware. Own-ground caveat: the payment/access layer is SpaceX's platform, not his, so this is a revenue bolt-on, not infrastructure he controls end to end.

signals.title: Pi Durable: an open-source framework for agents that survive crashes and let multiple people steer one conversation
signals.summary: A ~15,000-line open-source framework applies durable-execution patterns (checkpoint/resume, one harness running many conversations concurrently, live code updates mid-run) specifically to agent harnesses, including coding agents. Multiple clients can watch, join, and steer the same running agent conversation at once.

signals.title: Magnitude: a desktop app that auto-tunes local model inference per-device, 2x faster than llama.cpp
signals.summary: YC S25 launch (194 HN points): compiles and tunes inference kernels on your specific device rather than shipping precompiled ones, claiming up to 2x over llama.cpp, and plugs into existing agents (Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Cline) with zero token cost. Apache 2.0.

signals.title: The frontier price/speed war keeps compounding: GPT-6.1 Sol, Sonnet 5.5, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash all shipped the same week
signals.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches flagship GPT-6 Astra at lower cost (error rate down to 7.7% from 11.4%), Anthropic shipped Sonnet 5.5 at 30% faster/30% cheaper, and DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash, all in the same week. Incremental individually, but the compounding cadence is the story.

signals.title: Ruby on Rails creator DHH says his company is dropping hand-coding for AI, reignites the debate
signals.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson announced his company is moving away from hand-written code toward AI-driven development, reigniting a long-running industry argument. Not a new capability, a adoption/sentiment signal.

signals.title: Germany's RobCo hits $1B valuation, Europe's new robotics unicorn
signals.summary: RobCo (modular industrial robotics) crossed a $1B valuation. Later-stage than the seed-stage watch domain targets, logged for context, not a fit.

signals.title: Broadcom amasses $60B to fund chips for Anthropic
signals.summary: Macro infrastructure signal: Broadcom securing large-scale financing to build semiconductor capacity for Anthropic. Backdrop for frontier-model capacity growth, not an actionable signal on its own.

signals.title: Climate-tech subwatch: Fervo's enhanced geothermal plant is the week's notable hardware story, no flagship seed launch
signals.summary: Fervo Energy's Cape Station, the first enhanced geothermal plant, went from groundbreaking to commercial operation in 23 months. Notable execution speed, but Fervo is well past seed stage; climate subwatch again found no new early-stage flagship this week.
